thread:
Alyssa Chen: ping — customer on enterprise Dedicated. They send a rerank request and get HTTP 200 but every candidate score is 0. Customer thinks it started after they updated our client lib which 'flattens' passages into docs. Payload attached below.

Samir Patel: can you paste the exact request body they sent? quick guess: query field got nested inside each doc/candidate so the service treats it as metadata, not the ranking query.

Alyssa Chen: here's the minimal repro they gave (copied):
```json
{
  "collection": "kb-123",
  "docs": [
    {"id": "d1", "text": "...", "query": "how do i reset token"},
    {"id": "d2", "text": "...", "query": "how do i reset token"}
  ]
}
```

Jordan Lee: yup that's the cause. Our rerank API expects a top-level "query" (or "query" inside a separate request-level field) to compare against candidates/docs/passages. If each doc has its own "query", we treat it as a field to be ranked on, not the input query — leading to degenerate scoring.

Kai Nguyen: to add: client libs that try to be helpful by hoisting or duplicating request fields into each candidate can accidentally shadow the top-level query. Also if the SDK converts a single "query" string into an array and then merges, it can move it under docs[].query.

Alyssa Chen: customer says they used our Node SDK v1.4.2. They updated to 1.5.0 which introduced implicit "flattenPassages" option in the request constructor. They didn't notice so their front end now sends query per-doc.

Samir Patel: immediate workaround for customer: move the query to the root of the request. Example corrected payload: 
```json
{
  "collection": "kb-123",
  "query": "how do i reset token",
  "candidates": [
    {"id": "d1", "text": "..."},
    {"id": "d2", "text": "..."}
  ]
}
```

Jordan Lee: Also check they aren't hitting the result size limit. If they send 0-length candidate arrays or the SDK filters items, scores may be defaulted. But the payload above explains the symptom.

Alyssa Chen: customer confirmed switching to top-level query returns sensible scores. They asked if we can detect and warn when "query" appears inside candidates/docs/passages.

Jordan Lee: filed a small telemetry check: when we receive a request with top-level query missing and docs/candidates each containing identical "query" strings, we should log a warning and return a helpful 400 with guidance. I've opened ENG-ML ticket #RL-1298.

Kai Nguyen: repro steps for eng: 1) use Node SDK 1.5.0 with flattenPassages true 2) build payload that copies request.query into docs[].query 3) call /v1/rerank 4) observe all scores ~ 0 in our logs and client body 200 but no meaningful ranking. Attached request_id from customer: r-88f3b2.

repro-bot: automated note — copied logs for r-88f3b2 into ENG-ML channel. Trace: rerank_handler -> ranking_model -> fallback_zero_score_path (seen 2026-11-23 14:01:05 UTC).

Samir Patel: plan: ship validation in next patch (backwards-compatible): if top-level query missing and we detect identical per-candidate query strings, return 400 with message "Move your query to request root or use 'query' param; per-candidate query fields are treated as metadata. Workaround: downgrade Node SDK to 1.4.x or explicitly set flattenPassages=false.

Alyssa Chen: customer accepted workaround and wants ETA. Samir — can you add ETA to RL-1298?

Samir Patel: will do. ETA for validation patch: 5 business days. I'll also add an error message snippet for docs and update docs.rw/guide/rerank-schema.md.

Kai Nguyen: note for support: if customer still sees zeros after moving query top-level, ask for full request_id + small repro; also check if candidates are empty OR if they passed a numeric threshold that filters out all items.

Alyssa Chen: thanks team, marking resolved for the customer with workaround. I'll follow up when RL-1298 lands. :thumbsup:
